Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 16, verse 2:

Faith (al-Iman), submission (al-Islam), the Qur'an and striving in the way of God (al-Jihad) give life to the hearts, the good life, and the perfection of life is in Paradise. The Messenger is a caller to faith and to Paradise, so he is a caller to life in this world and the Hereafter. Man is in need of two kinds of life:

The life of his body, by which he perceives what benefits and harms him, and prefers what benefits him over what harms him. When this life is diminished in him, he suffers pain and weakness in proportion to that. For this reason, the life of the sick person, the grieving person, the one afflicted with worry, grief, fear, poverty and humiliation is less than the life of one who is free from these.

And the life of his heart and spirit, by which he distinguishes between truth and falsehood, error and right guidance, desire and misguidance. He chooses the truth over its opposite, and this life grants him the power to discern between what benefits and what harms, in knowledge, volitions and deeds, and grants him the strength of faith, will and love for the truth, and the strength of hatred and aversion to falsehood. So his awareness, discernment, love and aversion are in proportion to his share of this life, just as the living body's awareness and sensation of what is beneficial and what is painful is more complete, and its inclination toward the beneficial and its aversion from the painful is greater. The former corresponds to the life of the body, and the latter corresponds to the life of the heart. When its life is nullified, its discernment is nullified; and if it has some kind of discernment, it does not have the strength by which it prefers the beneficial over the harmful. Just as a person has no life until the angel, who is the Messenger of God, breathes into him from His spirit, so that he becomes alive by that breathing, although before that he was among the dead, so likewise his spirit and heart have no life until the Messenger breathes into them from the Spirit that was cast upon him. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, and He said: ﴿He casts the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, and He said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾.

So He informed that His revelation is a spirit and a light, and life and illumination depend on the breathing of the angelic Messenger. Whoever receives the breathing of the angelic Messenger and the breathing of the human Messenger attains both lives, and whoever receives the breathing of the angel without the breathing of the Messenger attains one of the two lives and misses the other. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose likeness is in darkness, never to emerge from it?﴾

So He combined for him light and life, just as He combined for those who turn away from His Book death and darkness. Ibn 'Abbas and all the commentators said: he was a disbeliever, astray, and We guided him.

He did not create that in vain. Rather, He created it as a creation that proceeds from the Truth, returns to the Truth, and contains the Truth. The Truth precedes its creation, accompanies it, and is its end. For this reason He used the preposition *bi* (with), which indicates this meaning, rather than *li* (for), which conveys the meaning of purpose alone. *Bi* conveys that its creation includes the Truth that precedes it, accompanies it, and is its end.

The preceding Truth is that these things proceed from His knowledge and wisdom. The source of God's creation and command, may He be exalted, is the perfection of His knowledge and wisdom. With the perfection of these two attributes, the product that proceeds from the one described by them is entirely wisdom, benefit, and truth. For this reason God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from the Presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾ (27:6). Thus He informed that the source of the receiving is the knowledge and wisdom of the speaker, and whatever is such is truthful, just, guiding, and instructive. Likewise, the angels said to the wife of Abraham when she said: ﴿Shall I give birth while I am an old woman, and this is my husband, an old man? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!﴾ They said: ﴿Thus says your Lord; indeed, He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ (Qur'an 11:72–73; the angels' reply is quoted here as in the source).

This refers back to His words "and [He] created," which means the creation of a child for her in old age. As for the accompaniment of the Truth to these created things, it is what they contain of wisdom, benefits, advantages, and signs that indicate to the servants God, His oneness, His attributes, the truthfulness of His messengers, and that His meeting [with them] is true, beyond doubt. Whoever contemplates existing things with the insight of his heart sees them as witnessing, speaking persons attesting to this. Indeed, their testimony is more complete than the testimony of mere report, because it is a testimony of state that does not admit falsehood. No intelligent, discerning person truly contemplates any creature without finding it pointing to its Originator and Maker, to His oneness, to the perfection of His attributes and names, to the truthfulness of His messengers, and to the truth of the meeting with Him, beyond doubt.

This is the Qur'an's method in guiding creation to reason from the various kinds of creatures and their conditions to establish the Creator, the Oneness [of God], the Return, and prophethood. Sometimes it informs that He did not create His creation in vain or without purpose; sometimes it informs that He created them with truth; and sometimes it informs them and alerts them to aspects of reflection and inference by which to affirm the truth of what His messengers reported, until it makes clear to them that the messengers only came to them with what they observe as evidences of its truth, and with what, if they reflected on it, they would see fixed in their innate nature and settled in their minds. And [it makes clear] that what they observe of His creation bears witness to what His messengers reported about His names, attributes, oneness, meeting, and the existence of His angels.

This is a great gate among the gates of faith, which God opens only for those for whom the precedence of felicity has been decreed. It is the most noble knowledge a servant can attain in this world.

(Section)

Consider how He (glory be to Him) unified the verse, from His saying ﴿He it is who sends down water from the sky; from it you have drink, and from it [grow] trees in which you pasture [your animals]﴾ to its end.

And He concluded it with the people of reflection.

As for the unity of the verse, it is because the locus of the proof is one: the water which He sent down from the sky, by which He brought forth all that He mentioned from the earth. Although its kinds vary, its source is one and its origin is one. So this is one category of His signs.

As for His specifying it for the people of reflection (fikr), it is because these creatures which He mentioned, arising from the water, are a locus of reflection (fikr), which is the heart's looking and contemplating, not a mere locus of looking with the eye. The beholder does not benefit from the mere sight of the eye until he moves from it to the looking of the heart, regarding the wisdom in that, its wondrous craftsmanship, and inferring from it its Creator and Originator. That is reflection (fikr) itself.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in the verse that follows, ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who use their intellect (ya'qilun)﴾, the plural "signs" is used because it comprises the night, the day, the sun, the moon and the stars, which are many signs differing in their essences, their creation and their modes. The darkening of the atmosphere at the setting of the sun and the coming of the night, which clothes the world like a garment and under which creatures rest, is a striking sign. Then the army of light arrives, preceded by the herald of dawn, so the army of darkness is routed, living beings spread out, and that garment is wholly stripped away: another sign. Then in the sun, which is the sign of the day, is another sign; in the moon, which is the sign of the night, is another sign; and in the stars there are other signs, as we have mentioned earlier. This is in addition to the signs accompanying them, such as the winds and their variations, and all the other things which God causes through them, which are further signs. So the context is one of plurality, and He specified these signs for people of intellect ('aql) because they are greater than what precedes them, more indicative and more significant. The first (signs) are like the kernels, and these are like the shells. Whoever derives proof from these signs and gives them their due indication deserves the description that befits the possessor of reflection, namely intellect. Moreover, the station of intellect comes after the station of reflection. So when He guided them by the first verse to reflection, He, by the second verse, which is greater than it, moved them to intellect, which is above reflection. Ponder this.

As for His saying in the third verse, ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember (yadhdhakkarun)﴾, He used the singular "sign" and specified it for the people of remembrance (tadhakkur). As for its unity, it is the same as the unity of the first, for what He has spread out on the earth, of differing substances, plants, minerals and animals, is all in one place. It is one of the categories of His signs, even though its types and kinds are many.

As for His specifying it for the people of remembrance, the Qur'an's method in this is to make His signs a means of insight (tabassur) and remembrance (tadhakkur), as He, exalted is He, said in Surat Qaf: ﴿And the earth—We spread it out and cast into it firm mountains and caused to grow in it every beautiful pair, as an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back (in repentance)﴾.

So tabassur is intellection ('aql) and tadhakkur is remembrance, and reflection (fikr) is the gateway and entrance to these. When one reflects, one gains insight; when one gains insight, one remembers. So the mention of remembrance in the verse comes in order following intellect, which follows reflection. He placed reflection first, as it is the gate and entrance; intellect in the middle, as it is the fruit and outcome of reflection; and remembrance last, as it is the goal sought from reflection and intellect. Reflect on this with true reflection.

If you say, what is the difference between tadhakkur and tafakkur? When the difference is made clear, the benefit becomes manifest.

I say: tafakkur and tadhakkur are the root of guidance and success, and they are the two poles of happiness. For this reason we have expanded on reflection in this respect, because of the great benefit and the intense need for it. Al-Hasan said: "The people of knowledge have never ceased to return from remembrance to reflection and from reflection to remembrance, and to speak to the hearts until they spoke, and behold, they had ears and eyes."

Know that tafakkur is the heart's seeking of what is not yet attained of knowledge from something already attained of it. This is its reality, for if there were no desired object that would be the target of reflection, reflection would be impossible, since reflection without an object reflected upon is impossible. Those materials are the matters already attained; if the sought thing were already present to him, he would not reflect upon it. Knowing this, the one who reflects moves from the premises and principles he possesses to the sought object he desires. When he attains it and it becomes his, he is reminded by it and sees the loci of doing and abstaining, what should be preferred and what should be avoided. So remembrance is the very aim and fruit of reflection. When he remembers, he returns with his remembrance to his reflection, and extracts what was not present to him. He continues to repeat, through his reflection, his remembrance, and through his remembrance, his reflection, as long as he is intelligent, because knowledge and volition do not stop at a limit; rather he is constantly traveling between knowledge and will. When you understand the meaning of the Lord's signs, blessed and exalted, being ﴿insight and reminder﴾, by which one gains insight out of blindness of the heart and is reminded out of its heedlessness: the opposite of knowledge is either blindness of the heart, removed by insight, or heedlessness, removed by remembrance. The purpose is to awaken the heart from its slumber by pointing to some of God's signs. Were we to pursue all of this, time would run out and we would not encompass the detail of a single one of His signs completely. But what cannot be grasped entirely should not be abandoned entirely. The best use of one's breaths is reflection on the signs of God and His wondrous craftsmanship, and moving from them to attaching the heart and aspiration to Him alone, rather than to any of His creatures.

The Garden will not be entered by anyone impure, nor by anyone who has any impurity in him. Whoever purifies himself in this world and meets God pure of his impurities enters it without any obstruction. As for whoever does not purify himself in this world: if his impurity is intrinsic, like that of the disbeliever, he will never enter it at all. If his impurity is acquired and incidental, he will enter it after being purified of that impurity in the Fire, and then he will leave it. Indeed, when the people of faith have crossed the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), they will be detained on a bridge between the Garden and the Fire, where they will be refined and cleansed of the remnants that were left on them, which had held them back from the Garden without obligating them to enter the Fire. Once they have been refined and cleansed, they will be given permission to enter the Garden.

God, in His wisdom, made entry into His presence conditional upon purity, so the one who prays does not come before Him until he has purified himself. Likewise, He made entry into His Garden conditional upon goodness and purity, so none enters it except one who is good and pure. Thus there are two purities: purity of the body and purity of the heart. For this reason it is prescribed for the one who has performed ablution to say after his ablution:

"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. O Allah, make me among those who repent often, and make me among those who purify themselves."

So the purity of the heart is through repentance, and the purity of the body is through water. When both purities come together in him, he becomes fit to enter into the presence of God Most High, to stand before Him, and to converse with Him in private supplication.

(Benefit)

The angels' greeting of peace and the good tidings were made to belong to them only on the condition of their dying in a good state. Thus the verse leaves no way for anyone who is not good to attain this glad tiding.

(Section)

As for the Iblisi and polytheistic Qadariyya, many of them have stripped themselves of the Sharia, are enemies of Allah and His messengers, and acknowledge neither command nor prohibition. This is an inheritance from their shaykhs, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿The idolaters will say: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything." Likewise denied those before them until they tasted Our might. Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring forth to us? You follow nothing but assumption, and you do nothing but guess."﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who associated said: "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything without Him." Likewise did those before them. So is there upon the messengers anything but clear notification?﴾ [al-Nahl: 35]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they say: "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 20]. And He said: ﴿When it is said to them, "Spend from what Allah has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom Allah could have fed if He willed? You are not but in clear error."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 47]. These are four places in the Qur'an in which He, glorified be He, made clear that invoking predestination as a proof is the act of the idolaters who denied the messengers.

The people have differed in their discussion of these verses into four groups:

The first group: they made these verses a valid proof, and that the one who argues by them has the proof against Allah. Then this group split into two sects: a sect that denied the command, the promise and the threat, and claimed that commanding, prohibiting, promising and threatening after this would be injustice, while Allah does not wrong any of His creatures at all; and a sect that affirmed the command, the prohibition, the promise and the threat, and said: this is not injustice. Allah disposes of His dominion as He wills, and punishes the servant for what he has no hand in, rather He punishes him for His own act, not the act of His servant, since the servant has no act, and the dominion is His, and He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked. Indeed, these disbelievers only uttered this statement which Allah related about them mockingly. Had they uttered it believing in destiny and predestination, and attributing all existing things to His will and power, this would not have been rejected upon them. The implication of this group's statement is that this is a valid proof if they said it in the manner of belief and not in the manner of mockery, so the idolaters would have the proof against Allah. And this statement is sufficient in its corruption and falsehood.

The second group: they made these verses a proof for them in refuting predestination, the general will, and destiny, for if the general will were valid, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had willed from them shirk, disbelief and the worship of idols, they would have spoken the truth and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would have confirmed them in it and not rejected it upon them. So when He described them with conjecture, which is lying, and negated knowledge from them, this indicates that what they said is not correct, and that they are lying in it, for had it been knowledge they would have been truthful in reporting it, and He would not have said to them: ﴿Do you have any knowledge?﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. This group also made these verses a proof for them in denying predestination, and claimed by them that there could be in His dominion what He does not will, and that He wills what does not occur, and that He has no power over the actions of His servants, whether men, jinn or angels, nor over the actions of animals; that He cannot cause anyone to go astray, nor guide him, nor grant him success beyond what He has done for him, nor protect him from sins and disbelief, nor inspire him with his right guidance, nor place faith in his heart; and that it is not He who made the one who prays a praying person, the righteous righteous, the wicked wicked, the believer a believer, and the disbeliever a disbeliever, but rather they are the ones who made themselves so.

This group shared with the group before it in casting war and enmity between the Sharia and predestination:

The first leaned toward predestination and fought the Sharia, and the second leaned toward the Sharia and denied predestination.

Both sects are astray, and one of them is more astray than the other.

The third group: they believed in destiny and predestination, and acknowledged the command and the prohibition, and placed each in its station.

So destiny and predestination are to be believed in and not argued by, and the command and the prohibition are to be complied with and obeyed. Belief in destiny and predestination is, in their view, part of the completeness of monotheism and of the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and standing by the command and the prohibition is required by the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. They said: whoever does not affirm destiny and predestination and does not stand by the command and the prohibition has denied both testimonies, even if he utters them with his tongue. Then they split over the interpretation of these verses into two sects: a sect said: what was denied upon them is their using the general will and predestination as evidence for His pleasure with it and His love for it. They made His will for it and His decree of it a proof of His contentment with it and love for it, for if He disliked and hated it He would have prevented them from it, for the wise, when he is able to repel what he dislikes and hates, repels it and prevents its occurrence; and if he does not prevent its occurrence, then either His power is lacking or His wisdom is lacking, and both are impossible with respect to Allah. So His love for what we are upon of worshipping others and of associating with Him is known. Those who said that Allah loves disbelief, wickedness and disobedience and is pleased with them agreed with these people, but differed with them in that He forbade them, commanded their opposites, and punishes for them, so they agreed with half their statement and disagreed with the other half. These verses are among the greatest proofs against the claim of both sects, and that the general will of Allah, His decree and His destiny do not entail His love and His pleasure with all that He wills and decrees. These idolaters, when they took His will as evidence for His love and pleasure, He rejected this from them, denied it upon them, and informed that they have no knowledge of that and that they are guessers and fabricators, for Allah's love of a thing and His pleasure with it is known only by His command to it upon the tongue of His messenger, not by the mere fact of His creating it. He created Iblis and his hosts, and they are His enemies, and He, the Exalted, hates them and curses them, and they are His creation. Likewise in actions: He created their good and their evil, and He loves their good and commands it and rewards for it, and He hates their evil and forbids it and punishes for it, and both are His creation, and to Allah belongs perfect and complete wisdom in His creation of what He hates and dislikes, of essences, attributes and actions, all proceeding from His wisdom and His knowledge just as they proceed from His power and His will.

The second sect said: what was denied upon them is their opposing the Sharia with predestination and repelling the command with the will. When the proof of Allah was established against them and His command and prohibition bound them, they repelled it with His decree and His destiny. They made destiny and predestination a nullification of the call of the messengers and a repelling of what they brought. Their brethren and descendants shared them in this, those who argue by destiny and predestination for sins and transgressions in half their statements, and they opposed them in the other half, which is their affirmation of the command and the prohibition.

So consider how these inheritances were divided among these shares, and how each people inherited their imams and predecessors, either in all of their estate, or in much of it, or in a part of it.

And Allah, by His grace, guided the heirs of His prophets and messengers to the inheritance of their Prophet and his companions, so they did not believe in some of the Book and disbelieve in some, but rather they believed in Allah's decree, His destiny and His all-encompassing, executed will, and that what Allah wills comes to be and what He does not will does not come to be, and that He turns hearts and directs them as He wills, and that it is He who made the believer a believer, the one who prays a praying person, and the God-fearing God-fearing, and made the imams of guidance guide by His command and the imams of misguidance call to the Fire, and that He inspired every soul its wickedness and its piety; and that He guides whom He wills by His grace and mercy and misguides whom He wills by His justice and wisdom; and that it is He who granted success to the people of obedience to obey Him, and had He willed He would have forsaken them and they would have disobeyed Him; and that He comes between the disbelievers and their hearts, for He intervenes between a person and his heart, so they disbelieved in Him, and had He willed He would have granted them success, so they would have believed in Him and obeyed Him; and that whomever Allah guides, none can misguide, and whomever He misguides, none can guide; and that had He willed, everyone on earth would have believed together, a belief for which they would be rewarded, accepted from them and pleased with them; and that had He willed they would not have fought one another, but Allah does what He wills: ﴿Had your Lord willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they fabricate.﴾ [al-An'am: 112].

Destiny and predestination, for them, have four levels, which their Prophet brought and reported from his Lord, the Exalted: The first: His prior knowledge of what they will do before bringing them into being. The second: the writing of that in the Reminder with Him before the creation of the heavens and the earth. The third: His will, which encompasses every existing thing, so no being goes outside His will just as it goes outside His knowledge not. The fourth: His creation of it, His bringing it into being and His fashioning of it, for there is no creator except Allah, and Allah is the creator of all things. So the Creator, for them, is one, and all else is created, and there is no intermediary for them between the Creator and the created. And they believe alongside this in His wisdom, that He is wise in all that He does and creates, and that the source of all of that is a perfect wisdom which required the proceeding of that and its creation, and that His wisdom is a true wisdom belonging to Him, established in Him like His other attributes, and it is not an expression of the correspondence of His knowledge to its object of knowledge and His power to its object of power, as the deniers of wisdom say, who affirm its word but not its reality. Rather it is something beyond that: it is the beloved end sought by Him, which is the object of His love and praise, and for its sake He created and fashioned, decreed and guided, caused to die and to live, made happy and wretched, misguided and guided, withheld and gave. This wisdom is the end, and the act is a means to it. So affirming the act while negating it is affirming the means and negating the ends, which is impossible, for negating the end entails negating the means, and negating the means, which is the act, entails negating the end, which is the wisdom. Negating the subsistence of the act and the wisdom in its agent is negating both in reality, for an act that does not subsist in its agent and a wisdom that does not subsist in the wise is something unintelligible. This entails denying His lordship and divinity, and this is a necessary consequence for whoever negates it, and he cannot escape it even if he refuses to accept it. As for one who affirms His wisdom and His acts in the manner that accords with reason and nature and what the messengers brought, no harm whatsoever follows from his statement; rather his statement is true, and the necessary consequence of truth is true, whatever it is.

The point is that the heirs of the messengers and their successors, owing to the completeness of their inheritance from their Prophet, believed in destiny, predestination, wisdom and praiseworthy ends in the acts and commands of the Lord, and stood by the command and the prohibition together with that, and affirmed the promise and the threat. They believed in the creation, whose completion of belief includes affirming predestination and wisdom, and in the command, whose completion of belief includes belief in the promise and the threat, the resurrection of bodies, the reward and the punishment. So they affirmed both the creation and the command, and did not negate either by negating their necessary consequences, as the Magian Qadariyya did and the Qadariyya who oppose the command with predestination. They were the happiest of people in the creation and the closest in kinship in this prophetic inheritance, and that is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

Know that belief in the reality of predestination, the Sharia and wisdom is not gathered except in the hearts of the elite of creation and the core of the world. The matter is not one of belief in the words of these designations while denying their realities, as many groups of misguidance do. The Qadariyya believe in the word "qadar," and some of them refer it to knowledge, and some refer it to the religious command and make His decree and His predestination to be the very same as His command and prohibition and the very same as Allah's will for the acts of His servants through His command to them to do them, and this is in reality the denial of destiny and predestination. Likewise wisdom: the Jabriyya believe in its word and deny its reality, for they make it the correspondence of His knowledge, exalted be He, to its object of knowledge, and His will to its object of will, so it is, for them, the occurrence of existing things in accordance with His knowledge and will. The denying Qadariyya are not content with this, but rise above it a level and affirm a wisdom additional to that, yet they deny its subsistence in the wise Agent and make it a created thing among His creatures, just as they said about His speech and His will. All of these affirm the word "wisdom" and deny its meaning and reality. Likewise the command and the Sharia: whoever denies the speech of Allah and says: Allah has not spoken and does not speak, nor has He said and does not say, nor does He love anything or hate anything, and all existing things are beloved to Him and what does not exist is hateful to Him, and He does not love, is not pleased, and does not become angry, and there is no difference in the reality of the matter between truth and falsehood, righteousness and wickedness, prostration to idols, the sun and the moon and prostration to Him; and He did not burden anyone with what he is able to do, rather all His burdening is with what cannot be borne and no capacity of the one burdened over it at all; and it is permissible that He punish men for not being women and punish women for not being men, and blacks for not being whites and whites for not being blacks; and it is permissible that He make a miracle appear at the hands of liars, and send a messenger calling to falsehood and the worship of idols, and command the killing of souls and all kinds of wickedness.

There is no doubt that this lifts the laws and the command and prohibition entirely, and had it not been for the contradiction of those who hold it, they would have been stripped of the religion of the messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. But their situation proceeds somewhat by means of their contradiction, and that is better for them than expelling their principles and acting upon their consequences.

The point is that none has believed in destiny, predestination, wisdom, the command, the prohibition, the promise and the threat with the true reality of belief except the followers of the messengers and their heirs. And destiny and predestination originate from the knowledge and power of the Lord.

For this reason Imam Ahmad said: "Qadar is the power of Allah." Ibn 'Aqil highly commended this statement from Ahmad, and said: he healed with this word and expressed clearly the reality of qadar.

The deniers of qadar are of two groups: a group that denied the prior knowledge and rejected it, and they are their extremists, whom the predecessors and imams declared disbelievers, and from whom the Companions disassociated themselves.

And a group that denied the completeness of power and denied that the actions of the servants are within the power of Allah, the Exalted, and declared explicitly that Allah has no power over them. So these denied the completeness of the Lord's power, and the other denied the completeness of His knowledge. The Jabriyya confronted them, coming with affirmation of power and knowledge while denying wisdom and mercy. For this reason the source of creation, command, decree and Sharia is from the knowledge of the Lord, His might and His wisdom. And for this reason the Exalted joins between these two names and attributes from these three often, as in His saying: ﴿And indeed, you receive the Qur'an from the presence of One Wise, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Naml: 6], and He said: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty﴾ [al-Zumar: 1], and He said: ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ghafir: 1-2].

And He said, in Ha Mim Fussilat, after mentioning the creation of the world: ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12].

And He mentioned a parallel to this in al-An'am, saying: ﴿He splits the dawn, and makes the night for rest and the sun and moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

So the connection of creation to His complete power requires that no existing thing go outside His power, and its connection to His complete knowledge requires His encompassing it and its preceding it, and its connection to His wisdom requires its occurrence in the most perfect and best forms and its inclusion of the praiseworthy end sought by the Lord, the Exalted. Likewise the connection of His command to His knowledge, wisdom and might: He is All-Knowing of His creation and command, Wise in His creation, Mighty in His creation and command. For this reason the Wise is among His Beautiful Names, and wisdom is among His Exalted attributes, and the Sharia proceeding from His command is founded on wisdom, and the Messenger sent with it is sent with the Book and the wisdom, and wisdom is the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ, and it includes knowledge of the truth, acting upon it, reporting it and commanding it, so all of this is called wisdom.

In a narration: "Wisdom is the lost property of the believer."

And in a hadith: "Indeed, among poetry there is wisdom."

So just as nothing that is decreed goes outside His knowledge, power and will, likewise nothing goes outside His wisdom and praise. He is praised for all that is in the universe of good and evil, with a praise He deserves for His essence, and from which His creation and command proceed. So the source of all that is from wisdom, and denying wisdom is in reality denying His praise. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 16, verse 36:

If it is said: What is the difference between His saying ﴿Among them are those whom God guided, and among them are those upon whom error was made due﴾ and His saying ﴿a group He guided, and a group upon whom error was made due﴾?

It is said: The difference is twofold, verbal and semantic. As for the verbal difference, the intervening elements (al-huruf al-hawajiz) between the verb and its subject in His saying ﴿upon whom error was made due﴾ (ḥaqqa ʿalayhimu al-ḍalālah) are more numerous than in His saying ﴿upon whom it was made due﴾ (ḥaqqat ʿalayhi). It has already been mentioned that omission (al-ḥadhf) is better when the intervening elements are numerous.

As for the semantic difference, the relative pronoun "man" (من) in His saying ﴿and among them are those upon whom error was made due﴾ refers to the nation and the community (al-ummah wa al-jamaʿah), and the word "ummah" is feminine in form. Do you not see that He says ﴿And We certainly raised up in every nation (ummah) a messenger﴾?

As for ﴿a group He guided, and a group upon whom error was made due﴾, the word "fariq" (group) is masculine. Had He said "fariqan ḍallū" (a group that went astray), it would have been without the feminine marker (tāʾ). The phrase ﴿ḥaqqa ʿalayhimu al-ḍalālah﴾ carries the same meaning, so it came without the tāʾ. This is a subtle feature of Arabic usage: the Arabs disregard the grammatical rule that a word would require when it stands in the meaning of another word that does not require that rule. You find them saying "huwa aḥsanu al-fityān wa ajmaluhu" (he is the best and most handsome of the youths), because it means "huwa aḥsanu fatan wa ajmaluhu" (he is the best youth and the most handsome of youths).

A parallel to this is their correct form in "ḥawl" and "waʿwar," because it means "aḥwal" and "aʿwar." Such examples are very numerous. If interpreting a word according to its meaning is acceptable in cases where analogical rule does not permit it, then how much more so where both analogy and usage permit it. Better than this is to say that they intended "aḥsanu shayʾin wa ajmaluhu" (the best and most handsome thing), and they put "al-fityān" in place of "shayʾ" to indicate that it is the best thing of this category. Had they limited themselves to mentioning "shayʾ," it would not have indicated the category by which the comparison is made.

This is clear proof that this guidance does not belong to him ﷺ, even if he were eager for it, nor to anyone other than God; and that when God, glory be to Him, leaves a servant astray, no one has any way to guide him, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Whomever God leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Whomever God wills to lead astray, He leaves him astray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path﴾. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him and who sees it as good [equal to one who is guided]? Indeed, God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself be consumed with regret over them﴾. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Have you seen one who has taken as his god his own desire, and God has left him astray knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and placed a veil over his sight? Who then can guide him after God? Will you not remember?﴾. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills﴾. And He says: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾. And He says: ﴿Have not those who believed despaired that, had God willed, He would have guided all of mankind?﴾. And He says: ﴿Whomever God wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾. And the people of Paradise say: ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this; and we would not have been guided had God not guided us﴾. They did not mean that some of the guidance is from Him and some of it from them; rather, all guidance is from Him, and had He not guided them, they would not have been guided. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Is God not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him. And whomever God leaves astray, there is no guide for him. And whomever God guides, there is no misleader for him. Is God not Mighty, Owner of Retribution?﴾. And He says: ﴿We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to make [the message] clear to them. Then God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills; and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾. And He says: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship God and avoid the Taghut." So among them were those whom God guided, and among them were those upon whom misguidance was deserved﴾. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and God leaves the wrongdoers astray, and God does what He wills﴾. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Thus God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him﴾. And He says: ﴿By it He leaves many astray and by it He guides many; and He leaves astray by it none except the defiantly disobedient﴾. And He says: ﴿By it God guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission and guides them to a straight path﴾. And He, glory be to Him, commanded all His servants to ask Him for their guidance to the straight path every day and night in the five prayers. This includes guidance to the path and guidance within it, just as misguidance is of two kinds: misguidance from the path, so that one is not guided to it, and misguidance within it. The first is being ignorant of it, and the second is being ignorant of its details, or some of them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 16, verses 38–39:

He, exalted is He, mentions two profound wisdoms in the resurrection of the dead after He has caused them to die:

The first: that He may make clear to people that about which they differed. This is an evident, visible clarification in which all creatures participate, whereas the clarification that took place in the worldly life is a clarification of faith, which was specific to some of them.

The second wisdom: that the one who falsified will know that he was a liar, even though he was upon falsehood, and that the attribution of the people of truth to falsehood was from his fabrication, his lying and his slander. Thus it will disgrace him with the greatest disgrace. So reflect upon the secrets of the speech of the Lord, exalted is He, and what the verses of the Glorious Book contain of profound wisdom, which bears witness that it is the speech of the Lord of the worlds, and which bears witness to His Messenger that he is the truthful one whose truthfulness is confirmed (al-sadiq al-masdub). All of this is part of the requirement of His wisdom and His praiseworthiness, exalted is He, and it is the meaning of His being ﴿the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them with truth﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 16, verses 38–39:

He, exalted is He, mentions two profound wisdoms in the resurrection of the dead after He has caused them to die:

The first: that He may make clear to people that about which they differed. This is an evident, visible clarification in which all creatures participate, whereas the clarification that took place in the worldly life is a clarification of faith, which was specific to some of them.

The second wisdom: that the one who falsified will know that he was a liar, even though he was upon falsehood, and that the attribution of the people of truth to falsehood was from his fabrication, his lying and his slander. Thus it will disgrace him with the greatest disgrace. So reflect upon the secrets of the speech of the Lord, exalted is He, and what the verses of the Glorious Book contain of profound wisdom, which bears witness that it is the speech of the Lord of the worlds, and which bears witness to His Messenger that he is the truthful one whose truthfulness is confirmed (al-sadiq al-masdub). All of this is part of the requirement of His wisdom and His praiseworthiness, exalted is He, and it is the meaning of His being ﴿the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them with truth﴾.

(Lateefah: On the singular "right" (al-yamin) and the plural "lefts" (al-shama'il))

Since the right side is the direction of goodness and success, and its people are the ones who are saved, it was given in the singular. Since the left side is the direction of the people of falsehood, who are the companions of the left, it was given in the plural in His words: ﴿from the right and the lefts﴾.

If it is said: why was it not likewise in His words: ﴿And the companions of the left—what are the companions of the left?﴾ Why did it come in the singular?

It is said: it came in the singular because what is meant is the people of this direction, and their destination and final outcome are to one direction, which is the direction of the left, the place of abode of the people of the Fire, and the Fire is on the left side. So it would not be fitting for it to come in the plural, because false paths, however many they are, their end is to return to the path of the Blazing Fire, which is the direction of the left.

Likewise its coming in the singular in His words: ﴿one sitting on the right and one on the left﴾ [the plural is not used here]: since what is meant is that every servant has two attendants, one sitting on his right and one on his left, who record for him good and evil. So for each servant there are guardians specifically assigned to his right and his left, and there is no sense in the plural here. This is unlike the words of the Exalted, quoting Iblis: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left﴾. Here the plural is used in correspondence with the large number of those he intends to lead astray. It is as if he swore that he would come to each one of them from before him, from behind him, from his right and from his left. It would not be fitting here to say "from their right and from their left" [in the singular], rather the plural here corresponds to the whole with the whole, which requires distribution across the individuals. Its parallel is: ﴿wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾.

Some people have said: the left is only given in the plural with regard to shadows, while the right is given in the singular, because a shadow, when it first arises at the beginning of the day, is at its greatest length, and so appears as a single shadow from the right side. Then it begins to shorten. But when it moves toward the left, it keeps increasing little by little, and the later part of it is other than the earlier part. So as it increases a little, it is other than what it was before, and each part of it becomes as if it were a shadow. Thus it is fitting to use the plural "shamā'il" in correspondence with the multiplicity of shadows. This is a good meaning.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 16, verse 49–50:

If it is said: What is the reason for the fear of the angels, when they are protected from sins, which are the causes of dread, and for the intense fear of the Prophet ﷺ, when he knows that Allah has forgiven him his earlier and later sins and that he is the nearest of creation to Allah?

It is answered: On this there are four responses.

The first response: This fear is in proportion to nearness to Allah and standing with Him. The closer the servant is to Allah, the more intense his fear of Him, because he is held to account for what others are not held to account for, and it is obligatory upon him to observe that standing and its rights, which is not obligatory upon others.

A parallel to this among observed matters: the one standing before one of the kings, who sees him, is more fearful of him than one far away from him, in proportion to his nearness to him, his standing with him, his knowledge of him and of his rights, and because he is required to render service and its duties in a way that is not required of others. So he is more deserving of fear than one who is far away.

Whoever grasps this properly will understand His ﷺ saying: "I am the most knowledgeable of you about Allah and the most fearful of Him," and will understand what he ﷺ said in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and others, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "If Allah were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them; and if He were to show them mercy, His mercy towards them would be better than their deeds."

What is meant is not that if He punished them He would be acting freely in His dominion, and one who acts freely in his dominion is not unjust, as many people suppose, for that would imply a kind of praise, whereas the hadith was related for the purpose of praise and to explain the greatness of Allah's right over His servants, and that if He were to punish them, He would punish them by His right over them and not without entitlement, for His right over them is manifold upon manifold what they have done. Hence he said after it: "And if He were to show them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds," meaning that His mercy towards them is not a price for their deeds, and their deeds do not equal His mercy; His mercy towards them is not in proportion to their deeds, since their deeds are not sufficient on their own to require mercy, and the rights of His worship and thanks that He is owed from them they have not fulfilled. So if He punished them in such a state, it would be punishment for His right, and He would not be unjust to them in it. Especially since their deeds do not match the least of His blessings upon them, so His many blessings remain without any return of thanks from them. So if He punishes them for neglecting to thank Him and for failing to render the right that is befitting for Him, He punishes them and is not unjust to them.

If it is said: When they do what is within their capacity of thanks and worship, then whatever else is befitting for Him is not within their capacity.

How then is punishment for it good?

It is answered from two aspects:

The first: What is within the servant's capacity he does not bring in its entirety; there must be lassitude, aversion, heedlessness and slackness. Moreover, even in the very act of standing in worship, he does not render it its due right of perfect vigilance, majesty, glorification and complete sincere advice to Allah within it, such that he spends all his capacity in beautifying and perfecting it outwardly and inwardly. So shortcoming is inherent both in the state of omission and in the state of action. For this reason, Abu Bakr asked the Prophet for a supplication to recite in his prayer, and he said to him: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You. So forgive me with a forgiveness from You, and have mercy upon me, for You are the Forgiving, the Merciful." He reported his wronging of himself, emphasizing it with the assertion that necessitates the establishment and realization of the report; then he emphasized it with the verbal noun that negates figurative and metaphorical usage; then he described it with abundance, which requires multiplicity and repetition; then he said: "So forgive me with a forgiveness from You," meaning that my deeds and my striving do not attain it, rather my deeds fall short of it, and it is only from Your bounty and kindness, not by my earning nor by my seeking forgiveness and repentance.

Then he said: "And have mercy upon me," meaning my only reliance is nothing but Your mere mercy, for without Your mercy destruction is certain for me. Let the discerning one reflect upon this supplication and what it contains of knowledge and servitude; and implicit in it is: if You were to punish me, You would be just towards me and would not wrong me, and I am not saved except by Your mercy and forgiveness. From this is His ﷺ saying: "None of you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and bounty." So if the servant's deeds are not sufficient on their own for salvation, then if Allah does not save him, He has not diminished any of his right nor wronged him, for there is nothing with him that requires his salvation, and his deeds are not adequate to thank Him for the little of His blessings. Would He then be unjust to him if He punished him? And would His mercy towards him be a recompense for his deeds, with the deeds being a price for it, despite his shortcoming in them and his failure to fulfil what is due of sincere advice in them, and the perfection of worship of modesty and vigilance, love and humility, and presence of heart before Allah in the deed? Whoever knows this knows the secret of why acts of obedience are concluded with seeking forgiveness. In Sahih Muslim, from Thawban, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he sought forgiveness three times, and said: O Allah, You are Peace and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 17–18], so He reported their seeking forgiveness following the night prayer.

Al-Hasan said: They extended the prayer until the pre-dawn, and when the pre-dawn came, they sat seeking forgiveness from Allah.

And Allah, the Exalted, commanded His servants to seek forgiveness after the outpouring from Arafat in the Hajj, saying: ﴿Then depart from where the people depart, and seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 199].

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prescribed for one performing ablution that he conclude his ablution with monotheism and seeking forgiveness, saying:

"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, make me of those who repent often, and make me of those who purify themselves."

This and the like clarify the reality of the matter, and that every person is in need of Allah's forgiveness and mercy, and that there is no path to salvation without His forgiveness and mercy at all.

The second response: Even if it is supposed that the servant brings all that is within his capacity of obedience, outwardly and inwardly, what is befitting for his Lord, the Exalted, is beyond that and manifold upon manifold. So if the servant is unable to attain it, he does not deserve what is consequent upon it of reward. And what he has done does not match the least of the blessings.

So if the reward of the deed that is befitting for the Lord from His servant is withheld, that would be a punishment for him, and the Lord would not be unjust to him in this withholding.

And if He were unable to provide its causes, He would not be withholding from him a right he is owed, so He would not be unjust in withholding. So if He gives him reward, it is a mere charity and bounty from Him, which He bestows upon him; his deed does not earn it, rather it is better than his deed and more excellent and more abundant, and is not a compensation for it. And Allah knows best.

The third response to the first question: When the servant knows that Allah, the Exalted, is the Turner of hearts, and that He comes between a person and his heart, and that He, the Exalted, is every day engaged in some affair, doing what He wills and judging what He desires, and that He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, raises whom He wills and lowers whom He wills, then what makes him secure that Allah will turn his heart and come between him and it and cause it to swerve after he has been set upright? Allah has praised His believing servants by their saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 8]. Had it not been for the fear of deviation, they would not have asked Him not to let their hearts swerve.

And among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ was: "O Allah, Turner of hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience, and O Establisher of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion." In al-Tirmidhi, from him ﷺ, that he used to supplicate: "I seek refuge in Your might that You misguide me, You the Living who never dies."

And among his supplications: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You."

So he sought refuge in the attribute of pleasure from the attribute of wrath, and in the act of well-being from the act of punishment, and he sought refuge in Him from Him from two aspects. It is as if in his seeking refuge from Him there is a gathering of what he had detailed in the two preceding phrases.

For seeking refuge in Him from Him returns to the meaning of what preceded it, while including a noble benefit, which is the perfection of monotheism: that what the one seeking refuge seeks refuge in and flees from is only the act of Allah, His will and His decree, and He alone is the sole Decider. So if He wills evil for His servant, none can protect him from it except Him. He is the One who wills for him what displeases him, and He is the One who wills to repel it from him. Thus He, the Exalted, is sought refuge in from Himself with regard to the two wills: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is no remover of it but He﴾ [al-An'am: 17]. He is the One who touches with harm, and He is the One who removes it; there is no god but Him. So the escape from Him is to Him, the flight from Him is to Him, and the seeking of refuge from Him is to Him, for there is no lord other than Him and no manager of the servant besides Him. He is the One who moves him, turns him, and directs him however He wills.

The fourth response: Allah, the Exalted, is the One who creates the servant's outward and inward acts. He is the One who places faith and guidance in the heart, and who places repentance, turning back, turning towards Him, love, reliance and their opposites; and the servant at every moment is in need of guidance that Allah places in his heart and movements by which He moves him in obedience.

This belongs to Allah, the Exalted; He is its Creator and Decreer. Among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ was: "O Allah, grant my soul its piety, and purify it, for You are the best to purify it; You are its Guardian and its Master." He also taught Husayn ibn al-Mundhir to say: "O Allah, inspire me with my right guidance, and protect me from the evil of my soul."

Most of his ﷺ supplications include seeking his Lord's granting of success, His purification of him, and His employing him in what He loves. Whoever's guidance, righteousness and means of salvation are in the hand of another, who is its owner and disposer, who manages it as He wills, having no share in its affair, who is more deserving of fear from Him? Suppose He has created guidance for him at present; is he certain and knowing that Allah, the Exalted, will create it for him in the future and inspire him with his right guidance forever? Thus it is known that the fear of those brought near to their Lord is greater than the fear of others. And Allah is the One sought for help. Hence was the fear of the foremost (al-sabiqun) of losing faith, as one of the Salaf said: "You fear sin, and I fear disbelief."

And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say to Hudhayfah: "I adjure you by Allah, has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named me to you?" meaning among the hypocrites. He would say: "No, and I will not absolve anyone after you."

Narrated by al-Bukhari. He meant: I do not open this door to people asking me about it; and his intention was not that no one other than you was free of hypocrisy.
